title: Joins & Features Without Leakage
objective: After this lesson you will be able to merge orders/customers/products with cardinality validation, engineer RFM-style features with as-of discipline, and prove no leakage with temporal cutoffs.
why: Enriched data powers models — and joins are where row counts silently multiply (fanout) and futures leak into training (as-of violations). Merges with validate= guards plus row-count reconciliation plus as-of feature cutoffs make enrichment safe: every joined row traceable, every feature timestamped before its decision point.

blocks.text: `validate=` declares expected cardinality (`many_to_one` for orders→customers, `one_to_one` for lookups): violations raise instead of multiplying silently. Pre/post row counts reconcile (left rows preserved exactly for left joins); indicator=True audits match rates (how many found partners?). Unvalidated merges are fanout incidents awaiting discovery.

blocks.code:
import pandas as pd
from io import StringIO
orders = pd.read_csv(StringIO("oid,cid,amt
1,C1,100
2,C2,50
3,C1,75
"))
cust = pd.read_csv(StringIO("cid,tier
C1,gold
C2,silver
"))
m = orders.merge(cust, on="cid", how="left", validate="many_to_one", indicator=True)
print("rows:", len(m), "preserved:", len(m) == len(orders))
print(m["_merge"].value_counts().to_dict())

blocks.text: **Recency/Frequency/Monetary** features summarize customers: days since last order, order count, total spend — each computed **as of a cutoff** (features see only pre-cutoff rows). Post-cutoff data in features is leakage: training scores inflate, live scores collapse. As-of joins (filter ≤ cutoff before aggregating) plus a written leakage statement per feature set.

blocks.code:
import pandas as pd
from io import StringIO
csv = "cid,day,amt\nC1,2026-09-01,100\nC1,2026-10-05,75\nC2,2026-09-15,50\n"
df = pd.read_csv(StringIO(csv), parse_dates=["day"])
cutoff = pd.Timestamp("2026-10-01")
pre = df[df["day"] < cutoff]  # as-of: C1's Oct row EXCLUDED from features
rfm = pre.groupby("cid").agg(n=("amt", "size"), total=("amt", "sum"))
print(rfm.to_dict("index"))
print("C1 uses pre-cutoff rows only:", rfm.loc["C1", "n"] == 1)

blocks.text: Every feature set ships a **leakage statement**: cutoff rule, excluded columns (ids, post-decision timestamps, targets-in-disguise like 'refunded_at'), and the verification performed (temporal split re-run). Unwritten leakage discipline doesn't exist — reviewers can't verify what authors never stated.

blocks.title: Guard the merge
blocks.note: Run it: 3 rows preserved, 1 unmatched (C9 → NULL, the indicator's job), tiers gold,NULL,gold. Left-join semantics with explicit unmatched visibility — matches audited, never assumed.

items: validate= declares cardinality (violations raise); row counts reconcile; indicator audits match rates
RFM as-of cutoffs exclude post-decision rows; leakage statements per feature set
Unmatched keys surface as NULL + counts — audited, never silently dropped

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice merge and confirm preservation + unmatched count. (b) In Python, merge with validate='many_to_one' on the same data and report _merge counts. (c) Write the leakage statement for RFM features with cutoff 2026-10-01 (rule, excluded columns, verification).
hints: Python: left merge + validate + indicator counts (both/must all match or left_only explained).
Statement: features use rows < cutoff only; exclude ids/post-decision timestamps/targets-in-disguise; verified by temporal re-run.
exercise.why: Twin parity (JS mirrors merge semantics), guard mechanics (validate + indicator), and leakage writing (as-of rules stated) are the three enrichment disciplines.
exercise.code: # Merge pattern: validate= + indicator + count reconciliation, always.

quiz.q: Row count triples after a merge. First check?
options: validate='many_to_one' (or correct cardinality) + pre/post counts: fanout from a many-many surprise
quiz.explain: Count explosions mean cardinality violated: validate= raises instead of multiplying; counts isolate the offending join.

quiz.q: Unmatched left rows vanish silently. Fix?
options: Left join + indicator + unmatched counts audited (NULL handling decided explicitly per column)
quiz.explain: Vanishing rows hide coverage gaps: indicator surfaces match rates; NULL policies decide per column (drop/fill/flag).

quiz.q: Feature uses full-history recency including outcome window. Issue + fix?
options: Leakage: as-of cutoff excludes post-decision rows + written leakage statement; verify by temporal re-run
quiz.explain: Post-decision data in features inflates training scores that collapse live. As-of discipline with stated cutoffs, verified temporally.

summary: Guarded merges (validate + indicator + counts), as-of RFM features, written leakage statements. Enrichment safe by construction.
